live: Dice 1 onion and finely chop 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse a 400g tin of chickpeas.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika and ½ tsp salt for 1 minute.
Add 300g passata and the chickpeas. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick, crushing some chickpeas into the sauce.
Stir in 150g spinach until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Make 4 dips, crack an egg into each, swirl the whites slightly into the sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Warm 4 tortillas in a dry pan. Rest 2 minutes, add black pepper, serve from the pan.

live: Pasta: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil and cook 180g spaghetti for 9–10 minutes until tender with a slight bite. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain.

Halloumi: Meanwhile, cut a 225g block of halloumi into 1cm cubes and pat dry. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the halloumi for 3–4 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Tip onto a plate.
Sauce: Halve or roughly chop 4 tomatoes. Add them to the pan for 1–2 minutes until they soften and blister, then tip onto the halloumi plate.

Sauce: Add 1 tbsp olive oil if the pan is dry, then cook 3 grated or finely chopped garlic cloves for 30 seconds. Pour in a 400g tin of chopped tomatoes, stir in 1 tsp mixed herbs and a small pinch of salt (halloumi is salty). Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes until thickened.

To serve: Tip the spaghetti into the sauce with a splash of pasta water and toss until coated. Fold through the halloumi, blistered tomatoes and 10g torn fresh basil. Grind over black pepper and serve.

live: Chicken: Cut 4 boneless chicken thighs into thin strips. In a bowl, rub with 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, the juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp chilli flakes, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper. Set aside while the veg cooks (5–10 minutes is enough).

Veg: Cut 1 red onion into thin wedges and 2 bell peppers into thin strips. Halve or roughly chop 3 tomatoes. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until softened and starting to char at the edges, then lift onto a plate.

Veg: Add the peppers to the pan (another splash of oil if dry) and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft with charred edges. Add the tomatoes for 1–2 minutes until they blister and soften. Season with a pinch of salt, then tip onto the onion plate.

Chicken: Return the pan to high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning, until browned and catching at the edges and cooked through with no pink in the middle. Squeeze over the juice of ½ lime.

To serve: Warm 4 tortillas in a dry pan for 20–30 seconds per side until pliable and lightly spotted. Mix 100g yoghurt with the juice of the remaining ½ lime and a pinch of salt. Return the veg to the pan with the chicken for 30 seconds to reheat. Fill the tortillas with chicken and veg, top with yoghurt and 15g chopped fresh coriander, and serve.

live: Potatoes: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Halve 2 large baking potatoes (about 600g) lengthways. Rub all over with 1 tbsp olive oil and ¼ tsp salt and lay cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 30 minutes, until the cut sides are golden and a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
Filling: Meanwhile, finely chop 100g spinach and thinly slice 3 spring onions (about 40g). Coarsely grate 75g cheddar and finely grate the zest of ½ lemon.

Mash: Turn the potato halves over and let them cool for 2 minutes. Scoop the flesh into a bowl, leaving a 1cm shell. Mash with 20g butter, ¼ tsp salt and black pepper, then stir in the spinach, spring onions, 60g yoghurt, the lemon zest and two-thirds of the cheddar. Pile back into the shells.
Topping: Crumble 50g feta into a small bowl, toss with the remaining cheddar and ¼ tsp chilli flakes, and scatter over the potatoes.
Bake: Return to the oven for 8–10 minutes, until the cheese is melted, golden and bubbling and the filling is piping hot in the middle. For a darker top, finish under a hot grill for 2 minutes.
To serve: Serve 2 halves each, straight from the tray.

Spices: Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin and 1 tsp paprika for 1 minute until fragrant.

Liquids: Pour in a 400g tin of chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes, breaking them up, until slightly thickened. Add a 400ml tin of coconut milk, 200ml water, 1 crumbled stock cube and a drained 400g tin of chickpeas.

To serve: Season with ¾ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper and ¼ tsp chilli flakes. Ladle into 2 bowls and top with 10g chopped fresh coriander.

live: Potatoes: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut 400g small potatoes into 2cm chunks, toss in a large roasting tray with 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt and black pepper, and spread out in one layer. Roast for 15 minutes until starting to turn golden.
Onions: Turn the potatoes. Add 1 sliced garlic clove and 3 spring onions (about 40g) cut into 3cm lengths, and roast for 5 minutes more.

Salmon: Cut 200g broccoli into small florets and 2 tomatoes into wedges. Add to the tray and stir to coat in the hot oil. Make two gaps and nestle in 2 salmon fillets. Season the salmon with a pinch of salt and drizzle with ½ tbsp olive oil.
Roast: Roast for 12–15 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily in the thickest part, the broccoli is tender with charred tips and the potatoes are golden and crisp at the edges.
Dressing: Meanwhile, mix the zest and juice of ½ lemon with 1½ tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and black pepper.

live: Rice: If you have no cold leftover rice, rinse 150g long-grain or jasmine rice and cook in 300ml water: boil, cover, simmer on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread on a plate to steam off for 10 minutes until no longer steaming (fridge-cold overnight is better — Cloake). You need about 400–450g cooked rice.
Wok: Cut 200g broccoli into small florets. Finely slice 4 spring onions (about 50g). Beat 3 eggs with ½ tsp salt.
Wok: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the broccoli with 2 tbsp water for 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp and the water has gone. Tip onto a plate.
Wok: Return the pan to high heat until almost smoking. Add 2 tbsp olive oil, then the cold rice. Spread it out, then toss until every grain is coated and hot, 1–2 minutes.

Wok: Pour in the beaten eggs and stir furiously so most of the egg is absorbed into the rice (Ken Hom / Cloake). Keep stir-frying for 2–3 minutes until some grains begin to toast and caramelise at the edges. Return the broccoli and toss through.
To serve: Throw over the spring onions, grind black pepper, and serve immediately.

Oven: Bake for 25–30 minutes until the tomatoes are bursting and blistered and the feta is soft and golden at the edges.

Base: Finely dice 1 onion. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and half of 25g butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft but not golden. Add 1 crushed garlic clove for 1 minute, then 150g arborio rice; stir for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and glossy.

Stock: Add a ladle of the hot stock and stir often until absorbed. Keep adding a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18–20 minutes until the rice is creamy and tender with a slight bite. Add a splash of hot water if you run out.

live: Dice 1 onion and finely chop 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse a 400g tin of chickpeas.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp cumin and ½ tsp salt for 1 minute.
Add a 400g tin of chopped tomatoes and the chickpeas. Simmer for 8 minutes, crushing some chickpeas against the pan, until thick.
Stir in 150g spinach a handful at a time until wilted, about 2 minutes. Taste for salt.
Make 4 dips, crack an egg into each and swirl the whites slightly into the sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Warm 4 tortillas in a dry pan. Rest the pan off the heat for 2 minutes, add black pepper, and serve with the tortillas.

live: Koftas: Grate half of 1 onion and thinly slice the other half. Crush 2 garlic cloves and finely chop a 30g bunch of fresh coriander, keeping a small handful of leaves back. Put 400g minced beef in a bowl with the grated onion, garlic, chopped coriander, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp mixed herbs, ¾ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper. Work it with your hands for 2 minutes until it is a smooth, evenly mixed paste, then roll into about 20 small balls.

Fry: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the koftas for 3–4 minutes without moving them, turn and fry for another 3–4 minutes, then shake the pan for 1–2 minutes until browned all over and cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Tomato salad: Meanwhile, dice 2 tomatoes and toss them with the sliced onion, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt.

Yoghurt & chilli butter: Warm 200g yoghurt with a pinch of salt in a small pan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until just warm. Do not let it bubble or it will split. Melt 25g butter in a second small pan over low heat with ½ tsp chilli flakes and ½ tsp mixed herbs for 1 minute until it foams.

To serve: Warm 4 tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side. Spoon the warm yoghurt onto plates, pile the koftas on top, drizzle with the chilli butter and scatter with the reserved coriander. Serve with the tortillas and the tomato salad.

Veg: Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Cook 250g broccoli florets for 4 minutes over high heat, adding 100g spinach for the final 1 minute. Drain well.

Halloumi: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry 1 sliced red onion for 5 minutes. Turn up the heat, add a 225g block of halloumi cut into cubes (patted dry) and cook for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides.
Spice: Add 1 crushed garlic clove, 15g finely grated fresh ginger and 1 tbsp curry paste; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
